[IRET.6.2.1] **`linear_scan: false` overlay — alpha tests over known types.**
When the loaded DSC was compiled with `linear_scan: false`, all
`DS_RETE_ALPHA_EQ` and `DS_RETE_ALPHA_CMP` tests operate on scalar or
interned-string types.  The engine may use an optimized comparison
path for these types that avoids the `cmp_vals` switch statement when
the type is known at node-creation time.  Specifically:

- `DS_RETE_VAL_INT`: direct `int64_t` comparison.
- `DS_RETE_VAL_FLOAT`: direct `double` comparison.
- `DS_RETE_VAL_BOOL`: direct `bool` comparison.
- `DS_RETE_VAL_STR`: pointer equality (interned) for EQ/NEQ.
- `DS_RETE_VAL_STR` for CMP (single-pattern only): `strncmp` bounded
  by the slot's `capacity` ([LSTR.11.1]): N codepoints, at most 4N bytes.

The comparison path is a `may`, and libds does not take it: every alpha
test goes through the general `cmp_vals` comparison.
`DS_RETE_ALPHA_REGEX` tests are only present when `capacity` is
declared, and RE2 is linear in the input length ([LREG.8.1]), so a
regex test costs O(capacity × P) with both factors compile-time
constants — the property `linear_scan: false` needs.

This supplements, and does not replace, the base [IRET.6.2]
behaviour.
